items.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I started playing with Frank Sinatra. I did everything with him and Nelson Riddle for about 13 years.

ctx.x: How many years did you spend with the Basie band?

Well from ‘38 until 1950, then I went back and I got a studio job here at ABC, with Mitchell Ayres on the Hollywood Palace, and then I started playing with Frank Sinatra. I did everything with him and Nelson Riddle for about 13 years. I recorded a lot with Nat King Cole, Ella Fitzgerald. I’ve been blessed all my life. It seems like that I don’t know why I’ve been called to do records that like anybody could have done it you know.

Yeah, but like you stated, you had your sound. You must have developed a sound that people recognized and that when Frank Sinatra did a date, he knew who he wanted to hear behind him, as did Nelson Riddle.

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: we went on tour with Sinatra, a lot of times... I still record with him... I played with him six years... Made all the recordings with him

ctx.x: The singer was like an accompaniment to a band. Now you're an accompaniment to singers. It's a singer's era. This is the singer's era, right now. And I wouldn't say -- call all of them singers. This is just the screamers era. You know, because those who are making money now, to me, they're not good singers. They're not good singers. You can name them all -- you can count them all on both hands, the good ones coming up nowadays, you know. I think Streisand can sing. She's a newcomer. Just put Sarah Vaughn and Ella…

they had more -- it was something about them. They made better singers. But you take the singers now like, you know, Olivia Newton-John or Helen Reddy or -- I don't dig any of them. To me, you know, they're --

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I started making some records…I think the first record I made with Nelson was with Frank Sinatra... Then we became very close friends and he always wanted me on his albums.

ctx.x: I found a few notes but I was so busy listening to Art, all I could do was play the melody. Oh, what a monster he was, oh man. They’re still trying to figure out the things that he was playing back in those days, they haven’t figured it out yet. But as I said before, my career has been just absolutely--so many incidents have happened---just unforgettable, unforgettable. I never thought that I would be in the company with such stellar personalities that I’ve been in. Like when we first came out here in 1939 to…

big. His trio had been such a tremendous success. I used to go hear Nat down on 7th Street there some place where he had a trio in there. And I never thought that I’d make an album with him and after he really had such tremendous success, I made many records with him at Capitol. Well, Frank Sinatra, I fell with him for about 13 years, 10 years. And Basie is the reason why, because I had started with him and what little success I achieved, I can attribute that to meeting Count Basie, playing in his band.
